On the evening of the 19th, I had an appointment for a tooth extraction at 6:00 PM. I arrived and waited until I saw the doctor around 6:30 PM. I've never had a tooth extracted before. The doctor injected local anesthetic as usual, but I didn't feel much numbness. The doctor tried pressing and wiggling the tooth and asked if it hurt. I did feel pain and told the doctor. The doctor sounded surprised and tried again, but it still hurt. So, the doctor injected more anesthetic and tried again, but I was still in sharp pain. I told the doctor again, but she seemed displeased and replied, "What do you want, patient? I've already given you a lot of anesthetic. What do you want to do? If it doesn't work, I'll have to put you under general anesthesia." I understand the doctor's perspective; she might have thought I wasn't tolerating the pain. However, I believe everyone's pain tolerance is different, and everyone's anatomy is different. Maybe I was a case where the anesthetic worked slowly. But I wasn't okay with the doctor's displeased tone. It took a third attempt to wiggle the tooth before it finally worked. It still hurt, though not as much as the first two times I mentioned, but I was still trembling. In the end, the extraction was successful. But the doctor said it seemed like there might still be a broken tooth root remaining, but they couldn't find it. (At that time, the doctor was only looking for saline solution, which made me a little worried and feel a bit flustered.) But if there really was one, my body should push it up on its own. This is another thing I'm personally wondering about: maybe it's because my root is bent that it still hurts when I move it.
